claims.text: Explicitly incorporating configurational disorder into ab initio interatomic-potential models will significantly improve lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy relative to traditional simplified-disorder methods.
High-entropy alloys relevant to thermal insulation have complex, multielement disordered microstructures.
From room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures, phonon scattering is the dominant consideration for the proposed thermal-insulation measurements.
Explicit treatment of configurational disorder will provide enhanced resolution of atomic-scale force-constant fluctuations.
Explicit treatment of configurational disorder will provide enhanced resolution of lattice-distortion details.
Configurational disorder in high-entropy alloys produces force-constant fluctuations that scatter phonons.
Mass and strain-field fluctuations associated with alloying disorder increase phonon scattering.
Lattice distortion can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, thereby lowering lattice thermal conductivity.
Capturing disorder-related scattering channels permits more accurate evaluation of phonon lifetimes.
Phonon relaxation time affects lattice thermal conductivity.
Traditional DFT or empirical models do not fully capture the detailed effects of configurational disorder in high-entropy alloys.
The refined model will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error by a statistically significant margin.
The refined model will accurately identify alloys having lattice thermal conductivity below 0.5 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ at 300 K.
The approach is primarily applicable when disorder-induced phonon scattering dominates thermal transport.
The approach may be less reliable for compositions with extreme electron-phonon interactions.
The approach may be less reliable at very high temperatures because additional transport or scattering mechanisms prevail.
The magnitude of the expected accuracy improvement is uncertain because quantitative experimental benchmarking of disorder metrics in high-entropy alloys is limited.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires only a statistically significant improvement, whereas the example falsification threshold can require more than a 20% error reduction. A statistically significant improvement smaller than 20% could therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.
